term: A3 event identity, causal priority and modal witness scope
resolution: Possible causability concerns the same essential-state event, not merely an analogous transition with different states; it does not assert that every actual event actually has a cause. A prior explaining condition is not automatically an existing concrete individual at an earlier time. The first-transition contradiction requires that interpretation; actual bearer, concrete capability and temporal presence remain explicit correspondence obligations. All contingent things is nonrigid none-to-some scope, not the fixed collection of actual individuals or a member-to-whole causal inference. A possible Necessary Being conclusion and the subsequent de dicto modal suffix do not by themselves certify a SAME actual rigid individual. Existing Scenario/local-frame results require their own guarded hypotheses.
